I think about this year the same way I did last year, because nothing much has changed. My man works in town sometimes, my son too, so on these 6 mu it is mostly me. I cannot do everything with my own hands at busy times, so I keep things simple.

Stevia (甜叶菊) is what gives us cash money. The company sends people around and pays good price for the dry leaves. So I put 3 mu in stevia. The other 3 mu I do wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as everyone on our street. That way we have some grain for ourselves and the stevia for selling.

For stevia, I plant the seedlings in April when the ground is warm enough. The company sometimes gives us the seedlings. Before I set them out, I spread 2 bags of compound fertilizer (that 15-15-15 kind) per mu, and then when they are growing I give them 1 bag of urea per mu, split in two times. So that comes to maybe 20 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, 8 kg potassium per mu. Stevia needs water — I pump from the well 5 times through the season. If leaf-eating worms come I spray, maybe 3 times. Good year I get 280-300 kg dry leaf per mu.

For wheat, I plant in October after I rotary-till the ground. One bag compound fertilizer at planting, then topdress with urea at jointing when I irrigate. That is about 18 kg N, 8 kg P, 6 kg K per mu. I irrigate 3 times — before winter, green-up, and jointing. Spray for aphids and the head disease, 2 times. My wheat gives about 450 kg/mu.

For maize, right after wheat harvest in June I plant directly, no deep tillage — just rotary. One bag compound at planting, then urea once when it is knee-high. 17 kg N, 6 kg P, 5 kg K. Irrigate 2 times from the well, spray once for borer. Maize I get maybe 520 kg/mu.

I would rather put a little extra fertilizer than see the leaves turn yellow. A thin crop is the worst feeling. The fertilizer money is hard but a bad harvest is worse.
